presentation.label: SCENE MUTES
presentation.summary: Each scene can carry its own track mutes: engage the scene and the mutes change with it.
presentation.overview: Scene Mutes lets a scene set the track mutes. In scene edit (hold SCENE until it opens), FUNC + a trig key toggles that track in the edited scene's mute mask, T1 to T12 for the sound tracks and T13 for FX; the first toggle marks the scene as one that sets mutes. While FUNC is held there, the trig keys light for the tracks the scene mutes. Engaging a marked scene replaces the mutes with its mask; engaging an unmarked scene, or none, puts back the mutes from before the first scene. A mute changed by hand or by MIDI while a scene is engaged goes into that saved state too. CLEAR drops the edited scene's mask and mark, CLEAR ALL every scene's. Masks are kept with each kit in the project and saved at once. It is a port of MrScruff's rytm-mods 0018-scene-mutes, with his code unchanged.
highlights: FUNC + trig in scene edit builds a scene's mute mask.
Engaging the scene sets the mutes; leaving it puts the earlier mutes back.
Scenes engaged from the pads set the mutes (run on a unit); CC 92, NRPN and Overbridge go through the same routine and should work, not tested.
Masks are kept per kit in the project.
usage: Hold SCENE until scene edit opens (FUNC pressed straight after SCENE does not open it).
Hold FUNC and press T1 and T2: the scene now mutes BD and SD, and those keys light while FUNC is held.
Release SCENE, start the pattern and engage the scene (SCENE + its pad): BD and SD mute.
Disengage it: the mutes come back as they were before.

access.location: Scene edit: hold SCENE until it opens, then FUNC + T1..T13.
steps: Hold SCENE until scene edit opens; FUNC + a pad picks the scene to edit without engaging it.
Hold FUNC: the trig keys show the scene's mask.
Press T1..T13 with FUNC held to toggle tracks (T13 is FX): T1 and T2 mute BD and SD.

controls.name: SCENE (held) + FUNC + T1..T13
controls.doc: Toggles that track in the edited scene's mute mask and marks the scene as one that sets mutes; T13 is the FX track.

controls.name: SCENE edit <CLEAR> / <CLEAR ALL>
controls.doc: Also drops the edited scene's mask and mark, or every scene's.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, with core-ar2 0.7.
SCENE has to be held until scene edit opens before FUNC goes down.
While SCENE is held the module takes FUNC + trig in every mode, so grid record's trigless lock and step record's track preview are hidden until SCENE is released.
Kit copy and paste, SysEx kit transfer, COPY/PASTE SCENE and clearing a kit do not carry or clear the masks.
A kit change while a scene is engaged keeps the old saved mutes.
Overbridge's silent mute path is not followed into the saved mutes.

load.display: None in the audio path: runs on key presses, LED updates and scene or mute changes
load.conditions: Static: the sites are SceneEditView's key and LED handlers, its two clear actions, and the entries of the scene-engage and track-mute routines. Nothing is added to the audio, sequencer or tick paths. Not a measurement.

hardware.summary: On an Analog Rytm MKII with OS 1.74 (run T210, build SMH1: the Modwerk base for core-ar2 0.7 and this module), engaging a scene whose mask held T1 and T2 silenced BD and SD while RS and CH played, a hand mute while engaged was kept after disengaging, the mask survived a power cycle, and <CLEAR> dropped it. Iced-Cream listened to the takes.
limitations: Build SMH1, .syx 7bec08468757ca5ef2e9ad0afd9a1ee1d3c9922ad0adb3c6734b361d57d66740, also carried analoghealth 1.3 as the remote-key harness. Firmware was not read back from the device.
Not tested on a unit: <CLEAR ALL>, scene engage by CC 92, NRPN or Overbridge, kit changes.
sourceSha256 is the SHA-256 of src/scene-mutes.s as tested.

tests.summary: Hardware (run T210, OS 1.74, core-ar2 0.7): a scene with T1 and T2 in its mask silenced BD and SD when engaged and brought them back when disengaged, a hand mute while engaged was kept, the mask survived a power cycle and <CLEAR> dropped it. Emulator: the same in rytm-emu, where the base alone does nothing.
